Sect: @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat} (@UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.nyOuQ8xvZEiNEJbM]{Tzimisce}-patronized)

Revenants are not vampires. In the early Middle Ages, @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.nyOuQ8xvZEiNEJbM]{Tzimisce} elders began infusing the vitae of selected Eastern European noble families with vampiric blood over many generations, eventually producing hereditary lineages of human beings born with vastly extended lifespans and an innate affinity for certain Disciplines. A revenant is conceived, born, and dies of old age (eventually) like any mortal — he simply carries vampiric blood in his veins from birth rather than receiving it through ghouling or the Embrace.

More than a dozen revenant lineages emerged from the original experiments. Some were wiped out by the Inquisition or the Anarch Revolt; a couple merged into other families and lost their separate identity; rumor credits a few other clans (Assamites, Setites, @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.z724BOvqpVyxjr6o]{Giovanni}, @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.clans.JournalEntry.jaYCq9rVOh0I9NCN]{Tremere}) with quietly cultivating revenant lines of their own. In the Final Nights, four revenant families remain in meaningful service to the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.sects.JournalEntry.6868ee8c357f4b73]{Sabbat}: @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.revenants.JournalEntry.IoQt3QoDDJZ8X4dz]{Bratovitch}, @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.revenants.JournalEntry.wABwn8FJtAN2e88I]{Grimaldi}, @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.revenants.JournalEntry.ldyqw2o2gR45LxDO]{Obertus}, and @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.revenants.JournalEntry.lo3JcX4zfCMF8bOW]{Zantosa} (each documented separately in this compendium). The Tzimisce also produce two kinds of purpose-built, non-hereditary specialized ghouls — szlachta and vohzd — using related vitae-manipulation techniques; these are covered in their own entry since they are manufactured individuals rather than a breeding lineage.

What Makes a Revenant

  • Vitae: Each revenant produces one Blood Trait of weak vitae per night. It is far weaker than Cainite vitae: it cannot create ghouls, assist an Embrace, or forge blood bonds. It can fuel the revenant's own Disciplines, heal injuries, and temporarily boost Attributes. A revenant's Blood Pool is 10 Traits, plus one for every full century of age. Revenants have no generation — they cannot be affected by Dominate from Cainites, and can neither diablerize nor be diablerized.
  • Inherited Powers: Each family lineage grants a set of in-clan Disciplines (analogous to a vampire clan's) and a hereditary weakness comparable to a clan weakness. A revenant begins with one level in one family Discipline and may learn more at the costlier "out of clan" rate; revenants cap out at the advanced level and can only ever learn the first level of each Discipline, plus one more level per full century of age.
  • Path or Humanity: Each revenant begins with one Trait in a Path of Enlightenment (or, where the family permits, Humanity), typically advancing about one Trait per century.
  • Creation is generational, not ritual-in-the-moment: producing a true revenant family takes Tzimisce elders generations of Thaumaturgical ritual work (Stimulation of the Male's/Female's Essence to enable ghouls to breed revenant-potential offspring, then Protection of the Revenant Essence and finally Perfection of the Revenant Essence performed on children before puberty). Each stage requires the creating vampire to win contested tests against the Storyteller, and the whole process is rare, slow, and usually riddled with failure — which is why so much inbreeding runs through every family. Once a lineage's first child completes Perfection, no new outside ghoul bloodlines can be folded into that family; some families (notoriously the @UUID[Compendium.vtmlarp.revenants.JournalEntry.IoQt3QoDDJZ8X4dz]{Bratovitch}) still abduct and breed with outsiders purely for sport, since such unions cannot produce true revenant offspring.
  • Disposition: Generations of isolation and exposure to the supernatural leave most revenants alienated from ordinary humanity, predisposed toward a Path of Enlightenment rather than Humanity, and tolerant of (often enthusiastic about) extremity, incest, and violence that would horrify outsiders. A revenant can pass for mortal more easily than a vampire can, having breath and a pulse, but rarely shares mortal sensibilities.
